mariner — refactor plan

Source: plan.md

Target version: 0.2.0 (breaking). Branch: dev. Developed against R 4.6.1.

0. Decisions taken

Decision Choice Consequence
Source formats .qmd only. .Rmd support is removed outright, not deprecated rmarkdown is out of Imports, the input_ext branch is gone, and a .Rmd handed to process_file() or generate_reports() is refused with a message. Done in P2.5
Output formats pdf only (xelatex) mariner produces reports. The revealjs, html and typst blocks the vendored extension used to carry are deleted, along with the stylesheets, Typst bindings and slide geometry behind them — see §0.2
Theme delivery Vendor outright, once. The theme’s sources were copied from /Users/thomasreinke/Local-R/QMDThemes and mariner now owns them. There is no sync script and no ongoing relationship with that repo One install_github for students, works offline. mariner can change its own colours, marks and geometry freely
Token generation The generators came too. _brand.yml remains the only file where a hex is typed; the LaTeX preamble and the extension manifest are generated from it by data-raw/build-tokens.R Changing a colour is one edit and a rebuild, not two hand-edits that can disagree. test-no-drift.R fails if the committed artefacts are stale
Extension delivery Assembled on demand, never committed. mariner_build_extension(dest, theme) builds _extensions/mariner-<theme>/ from the installed package’s single copies Nothing under inst/ is a second copy of anything else. See §0.3
Logo sizing Derived from the image files, never typed _brand.yml names three marks; the pdf corner placement states a target height and the width follows from the PNG’s own pixel dimensions
Figure theming In scope for 0.2.0. The full ggplot2 layer is ported Page and figures share one palette
Folder structure Two folders plus the extension, created by .onAttach() when the working directory looks like a project root, and by mariner_setup_project() explicitly See §2. quarto_assets/ is gone — the finding in §0.4 removed the reason for it
Bundling backend zip::zip(), not utils::zip() No external zip binary needed on Windows, and an existing archive is replaced rather than added to. Done in P2.5
API surface Keep the three exported names, add arguments generate_reports(), process_file(), process_files() survive; new args carry format, theme, and directories
Function prefix Ported functions are renamed qmd_* → mariner_* theme_qmd() → theme_mariner(), scale_colour_qmd_d() → scale_colour_mariner_d(). See §0.1
R version Develop and test against 4.6.1; Depends: R (>= 4.2) CI matches (P9.4, done)

0.1 Why rename the ported functions

qmdthemes is installed on the development machine, and a student could plausibly end up with both. Two packages exporting theme_qmd() and qmd_colors() would mask each other with a startup warning and no indication of which one won. mariner_* also matches mariner_setup_project(), so the whole exported surface reads as one package.

The qmd- prefix survives inside the LaTeX preamble (\qmdseriesonegreen, \qmdlogowidth). It is a private namespace there and renaming it would touch generated output for no user-visible gain.

0.2 Why pdf only

The vendored extension arrived contributing four formats. Three of them are gone as of P2.5, and what went with them was not small: qmd-revealjs.scss (692 lines), qmd-html.scss (488), five shared SCSS partials, both Typst partials, zoom.js, the generated SCSS/CSS/Typst token files and brand-header.html, R/slides.R (231 lines of slide geometry), R/scss.R (the layer-assembly machinery) and mariner_plotly_theme().

The reasoning: mariner exists to turn a parameterized .qmd into a bundled report for a class, and a report is a PDF. Carrying three unused formats meant carrying the stylesheets, the dart-sass test dependency, the slide-geometry derivation and a four-value format vocabulary threading through theme_mariner(), mariner_fig_dims(), mariner_knitr_setup() and mariner_fonts_available() — all to serve documents nobody in the course writes. mariner_formats is now "pdf", and it stays a vector so a second target later is an entry rather than a signature change.

Everything deleted is in the git history at d21a35c. Restoring revealjs would mean restoring R/slides.R, R/scss.R, the two format stylesheets and the five partials, and re-adding the SCSS/CSS token generators.

0.3 Why the extension is a build output

The first shape committed an assembled inst/quarto/_extensions/mariner-baylor/ alongside the sources it was built from. That shipped every font twice (28 .ttf files in the tarball), every partial twice, and made “which copy is real?” a question the drift test had to answer.

Now inst/ holds exactly one copy of each thing:

inst/brand/<theme>/_brand.yml     hand-edited, the only place a hex is typed
inst/tex/                          _macros.tex, defn.tex — hand-written
inst/assets/fonts/                 14 .ttf + 4 OFL licences
inst/assets/logos/                 3 marks
inst/generated/<theme>/            brand-preamble.tex, _extension.yml
                                   — the ONLY build outputs, from build_tokens()

and mariner_build_extension(dest, theme) assembles those into <dest>/_extensions/mariner-<theme>/ at the moment one is needed — scaffolding a project, or preparing a render. test-extension.R asserts the assembled directory is complete (manifest, every include the manifest names, all 12 static font cuts, their licences, every logo slot) and that no basename appears twice under inst/.

Tarball went from 2.5 MB to 1.3 MB. R CMD check’s “installed package size” check is OK.

0.4 Where a document has to be rendered — settled empirically

This was the plan’s top risk, and the original answer was wrong. Measured, by building the layout and rendering it:

Layout Result
Document in a scratch subdirectory, _extensions/ one level up beside a _quarto.yml Fails. The format resolves fine — Quarto walks up for _quarto.yml. Then xelatex dies: The font "Lora-Regular" cannot be found
Document beside its own _extensions/ Works

The reason: brand-preamble.tex reaches the fonts through Path=_extensions/mariner-baylor/fonts/, and xelatex resolves that against the directory holding the .tex — the document’s own, not the project root. The logo goes the same way, silently, through \IfFileExists. (When revealjs was still in scope the same layout produced a 20 KB deck with every @font-face unfetchable and exit status 0 — a silent failure where the pdf one is loud.)

Consequences, all folded into the phases below:

  • quarto_assets/ and its _quarto.yml trick are deleted from the plan. There is nothing for them to do.
  • _extensions/ lives beside the documents, in reports/.
  • process_file() copies (or symlinks) the extension into its scratch directory, which is what mariner_build_extension() is for.
  • The risk “parallel workers colliding on quarto_assets/.quarto/” dissolves — each worker owns its scratch root by construction.
  • Paths containing spaces render fine on macOS; the whole experiment ran under …/scratchpad/ext test/. Windows is still open (P5.2).

1. Where the material came from

/Users/thomasreinke/Local-R/QMDThemes supplied _brand.yml, the LaTeX includes, the fonts and logos, and the R modules that became brand.R, contrast.R, palettes.R, scales.R, ggtheme.R, fonts.R and knitr.R. The SCSS, Typst and slide layers came across too and have since been deleted (§0.2). The relationship is one-time and closed: nothing syncs, and test-no-drift.R asserts the string qmdthemes appears nowhere.

Three hard-won facts from that repo are carried as comments in mariner, because each one is a render failure if forgotten:

  1. No fonts: block in _brand.yml. Quarto emits brand font declarations into a SCSS layer that Dart Sass then rejects. (Moot now that no stylesheet ships, but the brand file is still written this way.)
  2. Fonts are set in brand-preamble.tex, not in the pdf YAML. Pandoc LaTeX-escapes mainfontoptions, so Path=_extensions/… becomes Path=\_extensions/… and xelatex dies inside \setsansfont.
  3. fig-pos: 'htbp', not Quarto’s default H. With H, a figure that does not fit runs off the page and the footer prints on top of it.

Note on inst/rmarkdown/templates/. RStudio’s New R Markdown ▸ From Template dialog only discovers skeleton.Rmd. Since mariner is Quarto-only, that dialog is no longer the delivery route — templates move to inst/templates/ and are reached through generate_reports(template = …) and mariner_setup_project(template = …). skeleton.Rmd is already deleted; P6 moves the directory.

The folders

Created relative to the project root:

assets/        the built extension, assembled once — the source of truth
reports/       generated .qmd sources, their rendered PDFs, and _extensions/
zip_files/     the bundles handed to students

Three, not four. presentations/ went with revealjs.

assets/ is back, with a different job. The version §0.4 deleted was a render location — a directory with a _quarto.yml that documents would be rendered from. That idea is dead and stays dead: §0.4 measured it failing. assets/ is now a build cache. mariner_setup_project() assembles the extension into assets/_extensions/mariner-baylor/ once, and everything that needs one copies from there: reports/ at setup time, and each process_file() scratch directory at render time (P4). The alternative is walking the installed package’s inst/ for all ~20 files once per document, which for a batch of fifty reports is fifty unpacks of the same 1.3 MB.

reports/_extensions/ remains the copy xelatex actually reads, for the reason §0.4 gives: brand-preamble.tex resolves Path=_extensions/… against the directory holding the .tex, so the extension has to sit beside the documents. A student who hits Render in RStudio gets the same result process_file() does.

zip_files/, assets/_extensions/ and reports/_extensions/ are appended to the project .gitignore — all three are build outputs in a student’s project exactly as they are in this repo.

Naming. The mariner_dirs() element is zips; the directory is zip_files/. The element name is what appears in every default argument (mariner_dirs()$zips), and the directory name is what a student reads in the files pane, where zips looks like a typo.

Created on attach, not on load

.onAttach(), which fires on library(mariner) — not .onLoad(), which fires on namespace load and therefore also during installation and R CMD check. Creating directories from .onLoad() would write to the filesystem during a build, which is both surprising and, on a read-only library path, a failure.

The guard, in order:

  1. getOption("mariner.auto_setup", TRUE) — one option turns the whole behaviour off.
  2. The working directory must look like a project root: it contains an .Rproj, _quarto.yml, DESCRIPTION, or .git. A bare getwd() is not enough — someone starting R in ~ or / must not get folders there.
  3. Non-interactive sessions are skipped. Rscript in CI, a future multisession worker, and R CMD check all load the package, and none of them is a person opening a project.

What attach does is cheap: it creates two empty directories and says so through packageStartupMessage(). It does not assemble the 2.5 MB extension — that stays in mariner_setup_project().

Resolution order for the project root: explicit argument → getOption("mariner.project_root") → nearest ancestor containing .Rproj, _quarto.yml, or DESCRIPTION → getwd().

3. Phases

P1 — Vendor the Baylor theme, generators and all — DONE

The shape changed during execution. The original plan copied the built extension and guarded it with a hash manifest. That would have frozen the palette: the token files are generated upstream from _brand.yml, so without the generators a colour change means hand-editing files with nothing checking they agree. The generators came across instead.

What landed

  1. Sources vendored into inst/ — the theme’s inputs, not its outputs.
  2. Generators ported — R/brand.R, R/contrast.R, R/generate.R, plus mariner_path() / mariner_themes / mariner_ext_name(). Renamed qmd_* → mariner_* throughout.
  3. R/logos.R is new — not a port. png_dims() reads width and height from the PNG IHDR header in base R, and every placement derives its width from a target height. This replaced two hardcoded per-file widths.
  4. data-raw/build-tokens.R regenerates everything and prints the derived logo sizes for eyeball verification.
  5. Tests: test-no-drift.R (byte-compares every generated artefact against a fresh generation, asserts no literal hex outside _brand.yml, asserts nothing references qmdthemes), test-logos.R.

Verified by smoke render — a mariner-baylor-pdf document compiled, and xelatex’s log confirms all 12 static font cuts loaded from the vendored directory with zero font warnings, the logo embedded, and fontspec’s Path= arriving unescaped (the documented failure mode).

Closed since: .Rbuildignore covers data-raw/, and the tarball carries all 14 .ttf files and their 4 OFL licence texts. inst/rmarkdown/ is still present and P6 deletes it.

P2 — Port the remaining R theme layer — DONE

palettes.R, scales.R, ggtheme.R, fonts.R, knitr.R ported and renamed; ggplot2 and systemfonts added to Imports.

Verified end to end: a ggplot2 figure under mariner_set_theme() draws in Atkinson Hyperlegible with #017553 for the data, #154734 for the title and #dfe3e0 for the grid — every value reaching the figure from _brand.yml.

One fix beyond the port. systemfonts::register_font() refuses to shadow a family that is installed system-wide and reports the refusal as an error. Lora and JetBrains Mono are common enough to be installed already, so the ported code warned once per family and under-counted what was drawable — on a machine that was better equipped, not worse. “already exists” is now treated as success.

mariner_install_fonts() is new. cairo_pdf() and base pdf() read fontconfig and ignore the systemfonts registry that bundling populates, so mariner_fonts_available("pdf") is FALSE on a machine where the faces are merely bundled. The consequence in a PDF report: the body text is Atkinson/Lora via fontspec, which reads the bundled files by path, while every figure falls back to the device default. One document, two typefaces, and nothing saying so. theme_mariner() detects the gap and passes base_family = "" rather than requesting a face the device cannot measure — asking anyway gives zero-width text metrics and a collapsed panel layout — but falling back deliberately is still falling back.

mariner_install_fonts() copies the bundled .ttf files into the user’s own font directory: ~/Library/Fonts on macOS, ~/.local/share/fonts plus fc-cache on Linux, and on Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts plus a HKEY_CURRENT_USER registry entry per face — copying alone is ignored there, so the registry step failing is reported as a failure rather than glossed. No administrator rights needed anywhere.

It is never automatic — it is the one operation in the package that writes outside the project. P3’s mariner_setup_project() may offer it; .onAttach() must not.

P2.5 — Quarto-only, zip, one copy, pdf-only — DONE

Pulled forward out of P4, P5 and P6 because the first three items were blocking R CMD check, and the fourth changes what every later phase has to carry.

  1. .Rmd removed. R CMD check was erroring — Namespace dependency missing from DESCRIPTION Imports/Depends: 'rmarkdown' — because P5.5’s DESCRIPTION cleanup had landed early while @importFrom rmarkdown render was still in process_file.R. CI on dev was red. The input_ext switch, the rmarkdown branch, the skeleton.Rmd lookup and template_ext_with_dot are gone; .Rmd input is refused by message, and two tests assert the message rather than merely that an error occurred.
  2. zip::zip(). utils::zip() shells out to a binary a stock Windows install does not have, and it adds to an existing archive rather than replacing it — re-running a batch left yesterday’s stale entries inside today’s bundle. The result is checked rather than trusted.
  3. Asset duplication removed — §0.3.
  4. pdf only — §0.2.
  5. inst/html/ renamed to inst/js/ before it was deleted entirely: R itself uses inst/html for a package’s own documentation and R CMD check WARNs about anything else living there.
  6. test-process_files.R’s parallel case now skips under pkgload rather than failing: a multisession worker is a fresh process that attaches mariner from the library, which does not exist during load_all(). requireNamespace() is not the test — pkgload registers the namespace, so it answers TRUE for a source load; pkgload::is_dev_package() is.

State after P2.5: 247 assertions passing, 2 skipped (the parallel case, and the figure-metrics case where the fonts are not installed system-wide).

The exported surface: 51 → 27 exports

The theme-building machinery is internal and undocumented in the manual. Everything that generates an artefact (build_*, build_tokens, mariner_build_extension), reads the brand file (read_brand), or does colour maths (contrast_ratio, delta_e, cvd_*, hex_to_*, best_ink, darken_to_contrast, mix_linear, relative_luminance) is @noRd, as are mariner_logo_width() and mariner_register_fonts().

@noRd, not @keywords internal. The first pass used @keywords internal, which un-exports a function but still writes a help page — it merely hides it from the index. That left 22 .Rd files for functions no user can call. @noRd writes no file at all; the roxygen prose stays in the source, where the person who needs it is already reading. mariner-package.Rd is retained deliberately — it is ?mariner.

What stayed exported, and why each has to be:

Export Why it is public
generate_reports(), process_file(), process_files() The workflow. The reason the package exists
mariner_install_fonts() The user runs it, by definition
mariner_knitr_setup(), mariner_fig_dims() The template calls these. A template is a user-facing .qmd that runs in the student’s session, so an unexported helper would break every generated document
theme_mariner(), mariner_set_theme() Re-theming a plot, or theming one the defaults do not cover
mariner_colors(), mariner_pal() Reaching a brand colour by name instead of typing a hex
The 20 scale_*_mariner_*() functions mariner_knitr_setup() installs discrete and continuous defaults, but ggplot2 cannot infer ordinal, diverging or binned — those must be asked for explicitly
mariner_themes, mariner_formats Argument vocabularies, referenced in every theme = / format = default

P3 — Scaffolding and folder structure — DONE

Implemented in R/setup.R, with the copy helpers in R/utils.R and 49 assertions in tests/testthat/test-setup.R. Exports go 27 → 31.

State after P3: 295 assertions passing, 2 skipped (the parallel case, and the figure-metrics case where the fonts are not installed system-wide), 0 warnings from document().

Two failures worth recording, because both were the test suite being right:

  • test-no-drift.R caught the ported copy helpers arriving with comments that named the upstream repo. §1 says the relationship is closed, and the drift test enforces it against R/ as well as inst/. The comments kept the reason the path arithmetic is written the way it is and dropped the provenance, which belongs here rather than in the source.
  • auto_setup_dirs() returned a named character(0) when there was nothing to create, which is not identical() to character(). Fixed in the function rather than the test: the only consumer is the startup message, which prints the directory names, so the list-element keys were never doing anything.

  1. mariner_project_root(path = ".") — the resolution order in §2.

  2. mariner_dirs(root = NULL) — returns the named list list(assets =, reports =, zips =). Single source for every default path in the package; no other function composes these strings itself.

  3. mariner_looks_like_project(path) — the attach guard: does this directory contain an .Rproj, _quarto.yml, DESCRIPTION or .git? Exported, so the behaviour is inspectable rather than mysterious.

  4. .onAttach() — the three-part guard in §2, then mariner_dirs() creation plus a packageStartupMessage() naming what it made. Silent when the folders already exist, so the message appears once per project rather than every session.

  5. mariner_setup_project(root = NULL, theme = "baylor", template = "report", overwrite = FALSE):

    root = NULL, not "." as first drafted. "." would scaffold the working directory, while P4’s output_dir = mariner_dirs()$reports walks up to the project root — so running setup from a subdirectory would create folders in one place and write reports to another. NULL routes both through mariner_project_root().

    Two more deviations from the draft, both flagged in the source: template defaults to "simple_report" (the template that exists until P6 moves it), and the starter is validated before anything is written, so a mistyped name cannot leave three folders and a copied extension behind.

    • creates the three folders
    • calls mariner_build_extension(assets_dir, theme), then copy_dir_safe() into reports/ — assembled once, copied, not built twice
    • drops a starter .qmd into reports/
    • appends zip_files/, assets/_extensions/ and reports/_extensions/ to the project .gitignore
    • prints a cli summary of what was created vs. skipped
    • offers mariner_install_fonts() interactively, and never runs it unasked

  6. overwrite = FALSE never clobbers. copy_file_safe() / copy_dir_safe() ported from qmdthemes/R/use.R.

  7. Idempotent — running it twice is a no-op plus a message. A test asserts this, and a second test asserts .onAttach() creates nothing outside a project directory.

  8. Route all user-facing output through cli, replacing the bare message() calls in the three existing functions.

  9. ?mariner already documents mariner_setup_project(), which does not exist until this phase lands. Do not leave that dangling longer than P3.

P4 — Function refactor — DONE

State after P4: 320 assertions passing, 2 skipped (the parallel case, and the figure-metrics case where the fonts are not installed system-wide).

§0.4 now has a test. test-process_file.R renders a document declaring format: mariner-baylor-pdf against a staged extension. Until P4 nothing exercised the theme at render time — test-extension.R only checked that the assembled directory was complete, which is a different claim.

The inline-R finding, which cost the most. Item 1 said to “verify the rendered title is unchanged”, and the YAML round trip is not the test that does it. yaml::as.yaml() defaults to single-quoted style, where an inner quote is escaped by doubling it:

title: "`r paste('Report', params$chapter)`"      template
title: '`r paste(''Report'', params$chapter)`'    round-tripped

yaml.load() returns the identical string from both, so a round-trip assertion passes — and the document fails to render, because knitr pulls inline R out of the raw line before any YAML unescaping and evaluates paste(''Report''. The quoting style is part of the contract with knitr, not a cosmetic choice of the emitter.

The fix is a sentinel: inline-R values are replaced with a bare token before emission and swapped back double-quoted afterwards. The obvious tool, the yaml package’s verbatim class, does not work here — it suppresses quoting only for content the emitter considers plain, and a string starting with " is not plain, so a pre-quoted value comes back single-quoted around its own quotes.

Two smaller emitter findings, both silent failures:

  • yaml::as.yaml() writes an R double as 3.0. expand_grid(chapter = 1) gives a double, so a title pasting params$chapter rendered “Report.3.0.7”. Whole-number doubles are coerced to integer.
  • Logicals emit as yes/no, which are booleans under YAML 1.1 but plain strings under the 1.2 spec Pandoc follows — so keep-tex: yes would quietly stop keeping the .tex. yaml::verbatim_logical fixes it.

generate_reports()

  1. Replace the regex YAML rewriting. The current implementation walks lines, finds ^params:, and gsubes (\s*name:\s*).+. It breaks on: a param whose default is empty or null, a list- or multi-line value, a param present in params_df but absent from the template, and any --- inside a code chunk being mistaken for a YAML delimiter. Replace with: split front matter on the first two --- fences, yaml::yaml.load() the header, modifyList() the params entry, yaml::as.yaml() back.

    • Warn when a params_df column has no counterpart in the template’s params block, rather than silently dropping it.
    • Preserve the `r ... ` inline-R title values through the round trip — yaml::as.yaml() will quote them, which is correct, but verify the rendered title is unchanged.

  2. Filename generation becomes an argument. Report-{chapter}_{problem_numbers}.qmd is currently hardcoded in two places — create_one_file() and the return value — which can drift, and it silently produces Report-_.qmd for any params_df without those two columns. New argument file_name = "Report-{chapter}_{problem_numbers}", a glue template evaluated against each row; extension always .qmd. The function returns the paths it actually wrote, collected from the map — not recomputed. Add glue to Imports.

  3. New argument: output_dir = mariner_dirs()$reports.

    theme was dropped, by decision. The theming comes from the template’s own YAML, so generate_reports() does not touch the format: block — and with that settled there is nothing for a theme argument to do but validate a value it never uses. A no-op parameter in a documented signature is worse than an absent one. process_file() and process_files() do take theme, because they have to name the extension they stage.

  4. Use purrr::pmap_chr() rather than pwalk + recompute.

  5. Error clearly, listing available templates, when a template name is unknown.

process_file()

  1. Assemble the extension into the scratch directory. §0.4 is why. Symlink where the platform allows it and fall back to a copy on Windows without developer mode; 2.5 MB per render is worth measuring before deciding the default. mariner_build_extension() already does the copy half.

  2. Add an assets_dir argument, defaulting to mariner_dirs()$assets, so a caller points at the extension P3 already built rather than rebuilding one per file. This is the reason assets/ exists — see §2.

  3. output_zip defaults into zip_files/, not beside the source. The root is resolved from the input file’s directory, not from getwd(): reports/ch1.qmd belongs to the project containing reports/ whatever directory R is sitting in, and a parallel worker’s working directory is not the caller’s at all. process_files(output_dir = NULL) passes the NULL through rather than resolving it once in the parent, so a batch spanning two projects lands each bundle in its own zip_files/.

  4. fs::dir_ls() is non-recursive; the file collection is now explicit and zip::zip(recurse = TRUE) reaches into _files/.

  5. New include argument controlling which of c("source", "script", "output", "intermediates") are bundled, defaulting to all four.

    <stem>_files/ is classed as output, not intermediates. For html it is not optional — the document is broken without it; for pdf it is merely redundant. Being wrong in the first direction ships a broken deliverable, being wrong in the second ships a slightly larger zip, so the classification takes the safe side. Anything unrecognised falls to intermediates rather than being dropped.

    The extension is never bundled — decided, not defaulted. Reports are rendered inside a project that already has one, and a copy per archive is ~1.3 MB each.

process_files()

  1. .progress = TRUE — furrr’s docs say it “will be deprecated and removed in a future version … in favor of progressr”. No warning fires today on furrr 0.4.0, so this is housekeeping rather than a fire: move to progressr::with_progress() when convenient.
  2. Fonts must be registered in each worker. mariner_register_fonts() populates a per-session systemfonts registry, so a multisession worker starts without it and its figures fall back — silently, because the parent process looks fine. Call it inside the worker function, not once in the parent. (.onLoad() does call it, which covers the common case; assert it rather than assume it.)
  3. Keep purrr::possibly() NA-on-failure semantics, but collect and report the actual error messages at the end instead of discarding them.
  4. Per-worker scratch roots come free from P4/process_file item 1.

P5 — Cross-platform hardening — DONE

State after P5: 383 assertions passing, 2 skipped (the same two as before: a multisession worker cannot attach a pkgload-loaded package, and the figure metrics case needs the fonts installed system-wide).

New files: R/preflight.R, tests/testthat/test-preflight.R, tests/testthat/test-paths.R.

The slugified output name, which was a real bug. Writing the space-in-a-path test turned up something the plan had not anticipated: Quarto does not name its output after the input stem, it names it after a sanitised form of the input stem. report with spaces.qmd renders to report-with-spaces.pdf and report-with-spaces_files/.

The PDF was fine — classify_artefacts() recognises it by extension. The _files directory was not: it was matched against paste0(stem, "_files") built from the input name, so it fell through to intermediates. Under the default include that is invisible, since all four categories are bundled. Under include = c("source", "output") it ships an HTML document without its dependencies — a broken deliverable, for a document whose only distinguishing feature is a space in its filename.

Matching _files$ by suffix instead is safe by construction rather than by luck: the scratch directory is created empty and receives exactly one file, so everything else in it came from the render.

The two font questions do not disagree — they are different questions. P5.2 asks for match_font() and mariner_fonts_available("pdf") to “agree”, and the first implementation reported a mismatch as “partially installed; restart R”. On this machine that message fired while all three families resolved and none were installed, which is not a stale cache — it is the ordinary state of every machine that has ever loaded the package. .onLoad() registers the bundled files with systemfonts, so match_fonts() finding them is mariner agreeing with itself. mariner_fonts_available("pdf") asks system_fonts(), i.e. what cairo_pdf() can actually reach. The check now reports that state for what it is, and check_fonts() takes both facts as arguments so its branches can be tested without asserting anything about the runner.

match_font() is soft-deprecated as of systemfonts 1.1.0 and warns once per session — which in a preflight would print a deprecation notice in the middle of the report it is writing. Switched to match_fonts(), and systemfonts (>= 1.1.0) is now the declared bound.

Two Windows bugs found by inspection, neither of which any macOS or Linux run would ever surface:

  • mariner_install_fonts() quoted its reg add arguments with shQuote()’s default, which is POSIX quoting — single quotes. system2() on Windows goes through cmd.exe, which does not strip those, so reg.exe would have received 'HKCU\Software\...' with the quotes as part of the key name and refused every write. Now shQuote(type = "cmd"). This is the step P5.2 named as “most likely to be wrong”; it was, though not in the way expected.
  • The registry value name was derived from the filename, giving Lora-Regular (TrueType). Windows writes <Full Font Name> (TrueType) taken from the font’s own name table — Lora Regular (TrueType). Close enough to look right in the registry, wrong enough to leave a duplicate entry when the same face is later installed through Explorer. windows_font_value_name() asks systemfonts for the family and style, and is a pure function over the file, so it is tested from macOS.

The Path= question resolved by inspection, not deferred. P5.2 worried that fontspec’s Path= might carry backslashes on Windows. It cannot: the path is a literal string in build_preamble(), never a file.path() call. There is now a test asserting no backslash appears in any Path= line, so it stays that way.

fc-cache absent on Linux is now reported rather than passed over. The install still works — the files land in a directory fontconfig scans, and it rebuilds when it next finds that directory newer than its cache — but it is not immediate, and a student told “installed, restart R” who then finds the fonts missing has no route from there to “this image has no fontconfig tools”.

What P5.2 still cannot answer from one machine. The three items needing a real Windows or Linux box remain open, and now have code to check rather than code to guess at: whether the corrected reg add actually makes the face visible to cairo_pdf(), whether fc-cache-less installs are picked up in practice, and whether mariner_fonts_available("pdf") flips to TRUE after an install and a restart. These belong with the CI runners in P9.

P5.5 became an invariant instead of a confirmation. The packaged template still loads tidyverse and conflicted, which P2.5 had removed from DESCRIPTION — so the render tests were passing only because this machine happens to have them. Both are back in Suggests, per the decision that packages the template loads get declared (the setup block is expected to grow — rstan and friends). template_packages() parses them out of the skeleton, and test-preflight.R asserts every one is declared, so the next package added to the setup block is caught at the moment the line is written rather than by a student on a clean machine.

template_packages() is textual, not parse()-based, and deliberately so: a .qmd’s chunks are not R code until knitr extracts them, other engines share the file, and inline `r ...` spans are not valid R in the surrounding markdown. Its one known miss — conflict_prefer("filter", "dplyr") naming dplyr in a string — is tested as a decision rather than left to be rediscovered: reading package names out of string literals would find "filter" too, and nothing calls conflict_prefer() without having loaded the package it arbitrates for.

mariner_check_setup() reports and does not repair, by decision. Every remedy is a copy-pasteable line. It is the function a vignette opens with and the one a student runs when something is wrong, and neither is a good moment to start writing to their font directory — mariner_install_fonts() already exists and already asks.

extension_manifest() / extension_missing() were added to R/extension.R rather than to the preflight, derived from the same EXTENSION_SOURCES list the builder walks. A checker with its own inventory goes stale the first time a font cut or a logo slot is added. This catches the half-assembled case a bare dir.exists() misses, which matters because xelatex does not fall back when fonts/ is short a cut — it aborts naming the font.

LazyData: true is gone, as planned. progressr and tinytex are in Suggests.

  1. Paths with spaces. The development checkout itself lives under …/OneDrive-Personal/Personal R Projects/mariner. Verified working on macOS (§0.4). Add a test that renders from a scratch directory containing a space, and normalise every path handed to Quarto with fs::path_real().
  2. Fonts — platform verification, which cannot be done from one machine:
    • Windows: does the reg add per-face actually make the font visible to cairo_pdf()? This is the step most likely to be wrong, and the one that silently does nothing if the value name does not match what Windows expects (<Font Name> (TrueType)).
    • Windows: xelatex resolving Path= with backslashes — fontspec wants forward slashes on every platform, so nothing may translate separators.
    • Linux: is fc-cache present in a bare container, and does the install still work without it?
    • All three: mariner_fonts_available("pdf") must flip to TRUE after installing and an R restart.
  3. mariner_check_setup() — a preflight the vignette opens with:
    • quarto::quarto_path() is non-NULL and quarto --version ≥ 1.4
    • a LaTeX engine is present (tinytex::is_tinytex() or a xelatex on PATH), with the exact tinytex::install_tinytex() line to run if not
    • the three font families resolve via systemfonts::match_font(), and mariner_fonts_available("pdf") agrees
    • zip::zip() round-trips a scratch file
    • the folders exist and reports/_extensions/mariner-baylor/ is present and complete
    • ggplot2 is present and theme_mariner() constructs without error Returns a data frame of check / status / remedy and prints it with cli.
  4. DESCRIPTION. Mostly done — rmarkdown, tidyverse, conflicted, svglite, plotly and utils are out; zip is in. Remaining:
    • add glue (P4) and progressr + tinytex to Suggests
    • drop LazyData: true — there is no data/, and R CMD build already says “Omitted ‘LazyData’ from DESCRIPTION”
    • keep tools in Imports; process_file() uses it
  5. Confirm every library() call in the template is satisfiable from Suggests, and that mariner_check_setup() reports any that are missing.

P6 — The report template

  1. inst/templates/report/skeleton.qmd — format: mariner-baylor-pdf. Carries over from the existing skeleton: the params block (chapter, problem_numbers, author), the computed title, the \newpage + Appendix with ref.label=knitr::all_labels(). The library(tidyverse) / conflicted / theme_set(theme_minimal()) setup block is replaced by:

    mariner_knitr_setup("pdf")

  2. template.yaml with name and description.

  3. Delete inst/rmarkdown/templates/simple_report/ entirely and move generate_reports()’s lookup to inst/templates/.

  4. mariner_templates() returns the available template names; mariner_template_path(name) returns the skeleton path. Both used by generate_reports() for its error message.

P7 — Tests

  1. Add skip helpers in tests/testthat/helper-skips.R: skip_if_no_quarto(), skip_if_no_latex(), skip_if_no_fonts(), skip_on_cran(). The current suite renders real PDFs unconditionally, so a machine without LaTeX gets failures rather than skips.
  2. Split fast from slow. Front-matter manipulation, path resolution, folder scaffolding, template discovery, and the whole colour layer need no renderer and should run in under a second. Only test-render.R renders.
  3. New:
    • test-setup.R — folder creation, idempotency, overwrite = FALSE protecting existing files, root resolution from a nested working directory
    • test-yaml.R — the param splice against awkward templates: empty defaults, null, list values, a --- inside a code chunk, a param in params_df with no counterpart in the template
    • test-render.R — one pdf end to end from a scratch directory built by mariner_build_extension(), plus the space-in-path case from P5.1, and an assertion that the fonts in the output are the bundled ones rather than a fallback
    • test-zip.R — bundle contents, that a failed render does not leave a truncated zip behind, and that re-running replaces rather than appends
    • test-parallel.R — two workers, asserting both bundles are complete and that figures in the parallel output are not zero-width. Needs the package installed; skip under pkgload::is_dev_package() as test-process_files.R already does
  4. Assert the error messages, not just that an error occurred. expect_error(process_file("nope.qmd")) passes for the wrong reason today. Done for the two .Rmd refusals; the rest of the suite still needs it.

P8 — Vignettes and examples

  1. get-started.Rmd — rewritten around the new flow: mariner_check_setup() → mariner_setup_project() → generate_reports() → process_files(). Every chunk that renders must be eval = FALSE or guarded — it currently calls generate_reports() and process_files() live, so R CMD build renders real PDFs on all three CI runners. Show pre-captured output instead.
  2. theming.Rmd (new) — mariner_colors(), mariner_pal(), the five scale families and when each applies, and the chrome-vs-data distinction stated plainly, because it is the one thing a student will otherwise get wrong (reaching for #154734 for a bar chart). Include the measured numbers from _brand.yml’s comments rather than paraphrasing them. Swatch plots make this vignette; it should be mostly figures.
  3. classroom-workflow.Rmd (new) — the actual use case end to end: a roster or problem-set grid in, a folder of per-student zips out. Covers parallel rendering, custom file_name templates, and what to do when one report in a batch fails.
  4. Examples in @examples stay \dontrun{} for anything that renders, but the colour layer is cheap and pure — mariner_colors(), mariner_pal(), mariner_fig_dims(), theme_mariner() — and should be live and runnable, so R CMD check exercises them. Same for mariner_dirs(), mariner_templates(), and mariner_setup_project() into tempdir().
  5. A short gallery: render the template once, commit the resulting PDF, and link it from pkgdown so someone can see what they get before installing.

P9 — Docs, CI, release

  1. README.md — install line, the folder picture, a 10-line quickstart, a figure showing a branded plot, and an “if it doesn’t work” section pointing at mariner_check_setup().
  2. NEWS.md — 0.2.0 entry. Started: the .Rmd removal and the zip change are written up. Still needs the pdf-only decision, the folder structure, the vendored theme and the new ggplot2 surface.
  3. _pkgdown.yml — a reference index grouped as Setup / Generate / Bundle / Colour / Scales / Theme, and all three vignettes in the navbar. Rebuild docs/.
  4. CI (.github/workflows/r.yml) — done. Matrix over macos/windows/ ubuntu at R 4.6.1, R CMD check via r-lib/actions/check-r-package@v2, covr::codecov() as a separate ubuntu job, Quarto and tinytex set up, triggering on dev as well as main. Still to add: a font-resolution smoke check so a Windows fontspec regression fails CI rather than a student’s laptop.
  5. Roxygenise, R CMD check clean on all three platforms, tag v0.2.0, merge dev → main.

4. Risks

Risk Where it bites Mitigation
_extensions/ not resolving from the render scratch directory — Settled — §0.4. The extension is assembled beside the document
Parallel workers colliding on a shared .quarto/ cache — Dissolved by the same change: each worker owns its scratch root
Font fallback silently degrading figures Zero-width text metrics collapse the panel layout; base pdf() refuses outright. Looks like a mysterious render failure, not a font problem P5.2, and mariner_check_setup() reporting mariner_fonts_available("pdf")
Fonts not registered in parallel workers Sequential runs look perfect, parallel runs produce subtly broken figures P4 process_files item 2, and test-parallel.R
Windows: xelatex and spaces in paths Students on Windows get render failures P5.1, P5.2, and the Windows CI runner
The port arriving with its comments stripped The constraints get rediscovered the hard way in six months The comments are the deliverable as much as the code
Generated artefacts going stale against _brand.yml A colour changes in one place and not the other; the page and the figures disagree test-no-drift.R byte-compares every artefact against a fresh generation
An assembled extension getting committed again Two copies of every font, and a stale one wins test-extension.R’s no-duplicate-basename assertion
YAML round-trip mangling inline R in the title Report titles come out literal P4 generate_reports item 1 — explicit test
The vignette rendering live during R CMD build CI fails on a runner without LaTeX, or takes minutes longer than it should P8.1 — guard the chunks

5. Suggested order

P3 → P4 → P5 → P6 → P7 → P8 → P9.

P5 stays ahead of P6 deliberately: the font registration and the path handling change what a template can safely assume, and it is cheaper to write the template once against settled infrastructure than to write it twice.

The two things worth doing first inside P3 are mariner_dirs() — because every later default path reads from it — and wiring mariner_setup_project() to mariner_build_extension(), which is the only piece of §0.3 that does not yet have a caller outside the test suite.
